what_its_for: Oxymetazoline is a nasal decongestant spray that helps relieve a stuffy or blocked nose caused by colds, allergies, hay fever, or sinus congestion. It works by shrinking the swollen blood vessels inside your nose so you can breathe more easily.
how_to_take: Blow your nose gently before using this spray. Tilt your head slightly forward and insert the tip of the bottle into one nostril while closing the other nostril with your finger. Squeeze the bottle and sniff gently at the same time. Repeat in the other nostril. Breathe in gently through your nose after using the spray. Do not spray into your eyes or mouth. Wipe the tip of the bottle clean after each use.
dosing: Adults and children 6 years and older: Use 2 to 3 sprays in each nostril no more than twice a day — once in the morning and once at night (every 10 to 12 hours). Do NOT use for more than 3 days in a row. Using it longer can make congestion worse. Children under 6 years old should NOT use this product unless directed by a doctor.
missed_dose: If you forget a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never use two doses at the same time or use it more than twice in one day.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and humidity. Do not freeze. Keep the cap on the bottle when not in use. Keep this and all medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT use this spray for more than 3 days in a row. Using it longer can cause 'rebound congestion,' which means your nose becomes even more stuffy when you stop using it. Avoid using it if you are already taking a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) antidepressant or have taken one within the last 14 days. Try not to share the bottle with others to avoid spreading germs. Avoid using extra doses to try to breathe better — more is not better and can cause side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get medical help if: your congestion does not improve after 3 days of use, your symptoms get worse, you develop a fever, you feel your heart beating fast or irregularly, you have difficulty sleeping or feel very nervous, you have high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid problems, diabetes, or an enlarged prostate — talk to your doctor before using this medicine, you are pregnant or breastfeeding, or your child is under 6 years old and you are considering using this product.
when_it_works: Oxymetazoline usually starts working within 5 to 10 minutes after using it. The effects can last up to 10 to 12 hours. Remember, it is only for short-term use — no more than 3 days.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Children: This product should NOT be used in children under 6 years of age. For children 6 to 12 years old, use only under adult supervision. Elderly: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially effects on blood pressure and heart rate. Speak with your doctor first if you have any heart or blood pressure conditions. People with certain health conditions: Do not use without talking to your doctor first if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, diabetes, thyroid problems, or an enlarged prostate, as oxymetazoline can make these conditions worse.
